slice.name: rmcp_tool_extractor_order_and_fail_closed_error

source_files.observation: ErrorData::invalid_request constructor verified in exact release content

slice.finding:
The released #[tool_handler] generated call_tool constructs ToolCallContext from the incoming RequestContext and request params, then calls ToolRouter.call. The released CallToolHandler adapters extract every declared handler argument via FromContextPart before invoking the registered tool body. RequestContext has a common FromContextPart implementation that clones the request context; Parameters

has a tool-specific FromContextPart implementation that deserializes tool arguments and returns ErrorData::invalid_params on failure. Therefore a registered tool declared with RequestContext and Parameters

receives both only after those extraction steps have succeeded, before body entry. The body can then immediately obtain the server-authenticated principal from RequestContext-derived HTTP Parts, evaluate current authorization, and return ErrorData::invalid_request(message, None) on missing/unauthenticated/unauthorized state before any persistent create-or-get or task materialization. This preserves router/typed-argument validation ahead of the first durable effect.
slice.scope_limit: This proves released extractor/body ordering and an exact fail-closed ErrorData constructor only. It does not prove HTTP middleware composition, persistent task create-or-get, restart redrive, or exactly-once external effects. ErrorData::invalid_request is a JSON-RPC INVALID_REQUEST rejection, not a distinct MCP authorization error class.
